maria (PM): Heads-up — enterprise customer emailed asking for a hard SLA: 95% requests under 120ms for our summarization endpoint + improved factuality checks. They want launch in ~3 weeks. Thoughts?
ken (Runtime): 3 weeks is tight. To hit 120ms we need a kernel change for attention caching + aggressive KV cache persistence for longer contexts. That’s a 2–3 week dev + 1 week perf validation. :thinking_face:
amelia (PM): @ken can we scope a reduced launch that meets the customer's requirements but with a phased rollout?
sam (Eng): technically we can do phased — ship a model variant with lower params (quantized) for latency and keep full model behind canary for quality. Runtime work still needed to avoid regressions.
alex (Infra): Reserved GPU pools for dedicated capacity take ~5 business days to provision in prod region if we already have quota. If we need extra PCIe networking or VPC peering to customer region, add another week. We can parallelize infra and runtime work.
jordan (Security): We'll need a quick triage: data flow diagram + PII checklist. If any customer prompt retention differs, we have to run a brief review with compliance. I can do the triage in 3 days if PM provides the exact data retention policy.
maria (PM): Customer accepts minimal retention (no prompts stored) but wants request/response audit logs kept on their side. I'll get them to sign the form today.
ken (Runtime): Proposed plan: 1) implement kernel cache patch (2w) 2) add quantized variant + perf runs (1w) 3) integration + canary (3d) 4) roll to 25% then scale. If infra provisioning overlaps we can still hit a soft launch at 3w with limited TPS, full SLA at 5w.
sam (Eng): Agreed. Also recommend adding an automatic fallback to a cheaper model if latency SLO is violated for >5% of requests in a 5m window. That reduces outage risk.
maria (PM): OK — product wants commit to canary plan and rollback criteria. Can we capture exact rollout config here?
ken (Runtime): Draft rollout snippet: ```
rollout:
  canary:
    fraction: 0.05
    duration: 72h
  thresholds:
    latency_p95_ms: 120
    error_rate_pct: 1
  fallback_model: model-v0.9-quant
```
alex (Infra): For infra I'll need the expected peak RPS for the canary and production. What's target TPS?
maria (PM): Customer peak expected ~60 rps sustained, spike to 200 rps. Start canary at 3rps -> scale to 50rps during perf window.
alex (Infra): Thanks. I'll request 2x p4d initially and autoscale to 4x for spikes. Quota ticket filed. ETA: 4 business days.
jordan (Security): After I get the data retention note: security review + cert check will take 48–72 hours. Need owner for CI secrets review. @sam?
sam (Eng): I can handle secrets review. I'll also add a small CI job to validate KMS access.
maria (PM): Can we set milestones and owners?
ken (Runtime): Runtime owner: ken — deliver kernel patch PR by 1815610000 (3 days from now), perf runs by 1815790000.
alex (Infra): Infra owner: alex — quota ticket and infra proofs by 1815530000 (4 days).
jordan (Security): Security owner: jordan — triage complete by 1815390000 (2 days).
sam (Eng): Integrations + fallback code owner: sam — integration tests by 1815700000.
maria (PM): Great. Customer-facing soft launch goal: 1815940000 (3 weeks). Full SLA target: 1818500000 (5 weeks).
deploy-bot: deploy window check: maintenance window open Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. Recommend scheduling canary start Tue 02:00 UTC.
ken (Runtime): One more note: kernel change modifies inference memory layout — must coordinate with infra to avoid mixed kernel versions in same pool. Suggest dedicate a small pool for canary to avoid mismatches.
alex (Infra): Will do. add pool tag = canary-181534.
maria (PM): Action items summary: - maria: get signed retention form today - ken: kernel PR + perf plan - alex: quota + canary pool - jordan: security triage - sam: fallback CI + integration tests. Everyone confirm ownership. :thumbsup:
ken (Runtime): Confirmed.
alex (Infra): Confirmed.
jordan (Security): Confirmed.
sam (Eng): Confirmed.
maria (PM): Thanks — I'll update the roadmap ticket and ping sales. If anything slips, call out ASAP. :eyes:
